packageRules.description: Every Go module update ships with the toolchain. `gomodTidy` raises go.mod's `go` directive whenever a dependency demands a newer language version, and that alone desynchronizes the three pins check-go-toolchain-sync.sh compares — so a module bump that travels without the toolchain cannot pass CI.

go.mod's `go` directive is a MINIMUM, so under the default `replace` strategy every newer Go still satisfies it and Renovate offers no update at all — which is why #83 moved aqua.yaml and the Dockerfile to 1.27.1, left go.mod on 1.26.5, and failed check-go-toolchain-sync.sh. `bump` is what makes the directive move with them.
Both Dockerfile base images: the golang builder stage (the second of the three Go toolchain pins) and the distroless runtime, re-resolved by digest together.
The third Go toolchain pin, as aqua spells it in aqua.yaml.

golangci-lint cannot cross a version skew with the toolchain: it refuses to run when its own build Go minor is older than the one the module targets (see the pin's comment in aqua.yaml), so it has to travel inside the toolchain's PR.

kind and kubectl move together: bumping kind changes the cluster's Kubernetes version (test/e2e/kind/kind.yaml pins no node image, so kind's digest-pinned compiled-in default applies), and kubectl tracks that node's Kubernetes minor.

aqua itself (the `aqua_version` the installer takes), the registry it resolves packages from, this config's own preset, and helm. None of them is coupled to the Go toolchain or to the e2e cluster, so they batch into one PR instead of one each.
The docs site's npm dependencies. Every one of them is exercised by the same `npm run docs:build`, so splitting them buys nothing but CI minutes.

mermaid is held below v12 by vitepress-plugin-mermaid, which declares `peerDependencies: { mermaid: "10 || 11" }` as of 2.0.17 — its latest release. `npm install` only warns and overrides that range, so a v12 lockfile can be written, but `npm ci` (what docs-lint.yaml runs) enforces it and fails the resolution outright, leaving the docs site uninstallable. Raise or drop this the moment the plugin admits v12; #98 is the update it blocked.
Workflow actions batch together; they share one validation — CI running at all.
